Also known as: CGEB. Before July 2026 it was called the GST/HST credit.
Who runs it: CRA – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). [1]
What it is: A tax-free payment every three months to help people with low and modest incomes pay for groceries and other everyday needs. [1] It replaced the GST/HST credit in July 2026. The rules are the same, and the amounts are 25% higher for five years (2026 to 2031). [2]
Who it's for: You must be a resident of Canada for tax purposes in the month before a payment and at the start of the payment month. [3]; You must be 19 or older. If you are younger, you can still qualify if you have (or had) a spouse or partner, or if you are a parent living with your child. [3]; You can qualify even if you had no income. [4]; The family income limit for a single person with no children is $60,012 (2025 income). Limits are higher for couples and families with children. [5]
Approximate amounts: Up to $679 a year for a single person, $890 for a couple, plus $234 for each child under 19 (July 2026 to June 2027). [5]; The amount goes down as family income goes up. You can be eligible and still get $0. [5]
Payment details: Four times a year: July, October, January and April. In 2026: July 3 and October 5. [6]
Application details: Most people do not apply. File your tax return every year, even if you had no income. [4] New to Canada? Apply for your first year with Form RC151 online (https://apps.cra-arc.gc.ca/ebci/uisp/rc151/ntr/en.html) (no children) or the Form RC151 PDF (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/rc151.html) and Form RC66 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/rc66.html) (with children). One application per household. [4,1]

Who runs it: CRA – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). [1]
What it is: A tax-free monthly payment to help families with the cost of raising children under 18. [1]
Who it's for: You live with a child under 18 and are the main person responsible for their care. [7]; You are a resident of Canada for tax purposes. [7]; You or your spouse or partner must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, protected person, registered under the Indian Act, or a temporary resident who has lived in Canada for the last 18 months and has a valid permit in the 19th month. [7,1]; People with a Refugee Protection Claimant Document are not eligible. [7]; If your child lives with you 40% to 60% of the time (shared custody), each parent gets half. [8]; When both parents live with the child, the mother is usually the one who should apply. [7]
Approximate amounts: Up to $8,157 a year for each child under 6, and up to $6,883 a year for each child aged 6 to 17 (July 2026 to June 2027). [8]; Families with income under $38,237 get the full amount. Above that, the amount goes down, and it can reach $0. [8]; Example from the CRA: one child under 6 and family income of $45,000 gives about $640 a month. [8]
Payment details: Every month, usually around the 20th. In December 2026 it is paid on December 11. [6]
Application details: Apply once with Form RC66 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/rc66.html). It also signs you up for provincial and territorial child programs. Newcomers may also need Form RC66SCH (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/rc66sch.html). [1] After that, file your tax return every year to keep getting it. [8] If your temporary resident permit is renewed, send the new permit to the CRA before the old one expires, or payments stop. [1]

Who runs it: CRA – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). [1]
What it is: A tax-free monthly payment for families caring for a child under 18 who is approved for the disability tax credit. [1]
Who it's for: You must be eligible for the Canada child benefit for the child. [1]; The child must be approved for the disability tax credit (DTC). [1]
Approximate amounts: Up to $3,480 a year ($290 a month) for each eligible child (July 2026 to June 2027). [8]
Payment details: Every month, inside the CCB payment. [8]
Application details: Apply for the child's disability tax credit with Form T2201 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/t2201.html). Once approved, the CRA adds this benefit to your CCB automatically. [8,9]

Also known as: CWB. It has two parts: a basic amount and a disability supplement.
Who runs it: CRA – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). [1]
What it is: A refundable tax credit for people who work and earn a low income. You get it through your tax return. [10] It has two parts: a basic amount for low-income workers, and a disability supplement for low-income workers who are approved for the disability tax credit. [10,11]
Who it's for: You must have income from work. [11]; You must be a resident of Canada for the whole year. [11]; You must be 19 or older on December 31, or live with a spouse, partner or child. [11]; If you were a full-time student for more than 13 weeks in the year, you cannot get it, unless you have an eligible dependant. [11]; The disability supplement is the second part of the CWB. It is not the same thing as the disability tax credit (DTC), but you must be approved for the DTC to get it. [10,11]
Approximate amounts: Up to $1,633 for a single person and $2,813 for a family (2025 tax year). [12]; The amount goes down as income goes up. A single person gets nothing above $37,742 of adjusted net income. [12]; Disability supplement (second part): up to $843 more. [12]; Amounts are different in Quebec, Alberta and Nunavut. [12]
Taxable details: Not stated in our sources. It is a refundable tax credit. [1]
Payment details: Once a year, as part of your tax refund. Up to half can be paid early (see the Advanced Canada workers benefit). [12]
Application details: Claim it on line 45300 of your tax return. Tax software works it out for you. [10]

Who runs it: CRA – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). [1]
What it is: Part of your Canada workers benefit, paid early in three instalments instead of waiting for your tax refund. [12]
Who it's for: Your last tax return must show you are entitled to the CWB. [12]; You must be a resident of Canada on the first day of each payment period. [12]; Payments stop if you leave Canada or are in prison for 90 days or more in a row. [12]
Approximate amounts: Up to half (50%) of your Canada workers benefit, including half of any disability supplement. [12]
Payment details: Three times a year: January, July and October. In 2026: January 12, July 10 and October 9. [6]
Application details: No application. It is paid automatically if your tax return shows you are entitled to the CWB. [12]

Who runs it: CRA – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). [1]
What it is: A non-refundable tax credit. It lowers the income tax that a person with a disability, or a family member supporting them, has to pay. [1] Being approved also opens the door to other programs, such as the child disability benefit and the CWB disability supplement. [9]
Who it's for: A medical practitioner (for example a doctor or nurse practitioner) must certify Form T2201 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/t2201.html), and the CRA must approve it. [9]; Approval can expire. The CRA tells you a year ahead on your notice of assessment. [9]
Approximate amounts: It reduces the tax you owe. It is not a cash payment on its own. [1]
Taxable details: Not income. It lowers the tax you owe. [1]
Payment details: Once a year, when you file your tax return. [1]
Application details: Fill out Part A of Form T2201 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/t2201.html), have a medical practitioner fill out Part B, and send it to the CRA. You can also apply online. [9]

Who runs it: Service Canada (ESDC) – Service Canada, which delivers this program for Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). [13,14]
What it is: A monthly payment for working-age people with disabilities who have a low income. It is run by Service Canada. [13]
Who it's for: You must be 18 to 64 years old and approved for the disability tax credit. [15]; You must be a resident of Canada for tax purposes, and you (and your spouse or partner) must have filed 2025 tax returns. [15]; You must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, registered under the Indian Act, protected person, or a temporary resident who has lived in Canada for the last 18 months. [15]
Approximate amounts: Up to $204.20 a month (July 2026 to June 2027). [16]; Some work income is not counted: $10,210 for a single person and $14,294 for a couple. [16]; The amount goes down as income goes up. [16]
Payment details: Every month, on the third Thursday. [6]
Application details: Apply to Service Canada (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/disability/canada-disability-benefit/apply.html) after your disability tax credit is approved. People who get a letter from Service Canada can use the application code in it. [17]

Also known as: CPP. You earn it by working and paying into the plan.
Who runs it: Service Canada (ESDC) – Service Canada, which delivers this program for Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). [18,14]
What it is: A monthly pension that replaces part of your income when you retire. It is based on the money you paid into the CPP while working. [18]
Who it's for: You must be at least 60 years old. [18]; You must have made at least one valid contribution to the CPP, from work in Canada or from credits shared by a former spouse or partner. [18]
Approximate amounts: Depends on your average earnings, how much you paid in, and the age you start it. [18]
Payment details: Every month, on the same day as Old Age Security. [6]
Application details: It is not automatic. You must apply to Service Canada, ideally before you want it to start. [18]

Also known as: OAS. Based on age and years lived in Canada, not on work.
Who runs it: Service Canada (ESDC) – Service Canada, which delivers this program for Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). [19,14]
What it is: A monthly pension for people 65 and older. You can get it even if you are still working or never worked. [19]
Who it's for: You must be 65 or older. [19]; If you live in Canada: you must be a Canadian citizen or legal resident when your pension is approved, and have lived in Canada for at least 10 years after age 18. [19]; If you live outside Canada: you must have lived in Canada for at least 20 years after age 18. [19]; To get the full pension, you need 40 years in Canada after age 18. With fewer years, you get part of it. [20]
Approximate amounts: If you are 65 to 74: up to $762.50 a month. [21]; If you are 75 or older: up to $838.75 a month. [21]; These amounts are for October to December 2026. They are updated every three months. [21]
Taxable details: Yes. It is taxable. If your 2025 net income was over $93,454, you may have to pay back some or all of it. [20]
Payment details: Every month, near the end of the month. In 2026: October 28, November 26, December 22. [6]
Application details: Many people are enrolled automatically and get a letter shortly after their 64th birthday. If you get a letter asking you to apply, or no letter, you need to apply. [22] Apply online or with paper form ISP-3550 (OAS and GIS together). See how to apply (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/publicpensions/old-age-security/guaranteed-income-supplement/apply.html). [22]

Also known as: GIS. An extra payment on top of OAS for people with low income.
Who runs it: Service Canada (ESDC) – Service Canada, which delivers this program for Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). [22,14]
What it is: A monthly payment for people who get Old Age Security and have a low income. [21]
Who it's for: You must receive Old Age Security and live in Canada. [21]; You must be a Canadian citizen or legal resident. [21]; You cannot get it while you are under a sponsorship agreement. [21]; A single person's income must be under $23,112. Couples have higher limits. [21]
Approximate amounts: Up to $1,138.90 a month for a single person (October to December 2026). [21]; Up to $685.56 a month if your spouse gets the full OAS pension. [21]
Payment details: Every month, with your OAS payment. [6]
Application details: Service Canada tries to enroll you automatically and sends a letter shortly after your 64th birthday. If you did not get a letter, or it asks you to apply, apply here (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/publicpensions/old-age-security/guaranteed-income-supplement/apply.html) (form ISP-3025 if you already get OAS). Benefit: Allowance and Allowance for the Survivor
Who runs it: Service Canada (ESDC) – Service Canada, which delivers this program for Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). [19,14]
What it is: Monthly payments for people aged 60 to 64 with low income whose spouse gets the GIS, or who are widowed. [21]
Who it's for: You must be 60 to 64, a Canadian citizen or legal resident, and have lived in Canada at least 10 years since age 18. [21]; Allowance: your spouse or partner receives the GIS and full OAS, and your combined income is under $42,768. [21]; Allowance for the Survivor: your spouse or partner has died, you have not re-partnered, and your income is under $31,152. [21]
Approximate amounts: Up to $1,448.06 a month (Allowance) or $1,726.18 a month (Survivor), October to December 2026. [21]
Payment details: Every month, on the OAS payment dates. [6]
Application details: Apply to Service Canada. [19]

Who runs it: Health Canada, with Service Canada – Health Canada leads the plan. Service Canada handles applications on its behalf, and Sun Life pays the dental claims. [14]
What it is: Helps pay for dental care for people who do not have dental insurance. It pays the dentist, not you. [23]
Who it's for: You must not have access to dental insurance. [14]; Your adjusted family net income must be under $90,000. [14]; You must be a resident of Canada for tax purposes and have filed last year's tax return. [14]; You must renew every year. [24]
Approximate amounts: No co-payment if family income is under $70,000. [23]; You pay a 40% co-payment if income is $70,000 to $79,999, and a 60% co-payment if it is $80,000 to $89,999. [23]
Taxable details: Not a cash payment. It is dental coverage. [23]
Payment details: Coverage for the benefit year (July to June), as long as you stay enrolled. [24]
Application details: Apply online (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/dental/dental-care-plan/apply.html) or by phone. Applications for July 2026 to June 2027 are open. [24,14]

Who runs it: Retraite Québec – Retraite Québec (Government of Quebec). [43]
What it is: Quebec's payment for families with children under 18. You can get it in addition to the federal CCB. [43]
Who it's for: You have a child under 18 who lives with you and depends on you. [43]; The amount is recalculated each July, using your family income and whether you had a spouse on December 31 of the previous year, from your Quebec tax return. [44]; Both you and your spouse must file a Quebec return every year by April 30, even with no income. If you file late, back payments are limited to 3 years. [44]
Approximate amounts: From $1,221 to $3,068 a year for each child (2026). [45]; Single-parent families get $430 to $1,077 more. [45]
Payment details: Four times a year: January, April, July and October. You can ask for monthly payments with the change-in-frequency form (https://www.rrq.gouv.qc.ca/en/services/formulaires/soutien_aux_enfants/Pages/changement_frequence.aspx). [46,47]
Application details: Automatic when a birth in Quebec is declared. [44] You must apply (https://rrq.gouv.qc.ca/en/services/services_en_ligne/soutien_aux_enfants/Pages/demande_paiement_sae.aspx) if you adopt, immigrate, move to Quebec, have a child born outside Quebec, or get full or shared custody. Also known as: Crédit d'impôt pour solidarité, from Revenu Québec
Who runs it: Revenu Québec – Revenu Québec (Government of Quebec). [49]
What it is: A refundable credit for households with low and modest incomes. It has three parts: housing, QST (Quebec sales tax), and one for people living in northern villages. [49]
Who it's for: It is based on your situation on December 31, 2025. [49]; No credit if family income is at or above $64,545 for a single person. Limits are higher for couples and families with children. [49]; If you live in a northern village, the income limits do not apply. [49]
Approximate amounts: Depends on which parts apply to you and on your income. Revenu Québec has an estimator. [49]
Payment details: $240 or less: one payment in July. $241 to $799: four payments (July, October, January, April). $800 or more: every month from July 2026 to June 2027. [50]
Application details: Fill out Schedule D (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/citizens/income-tax-return/completing-your-income-tax-return/how-to-complete-your-income-tax-return/line-by-line-help/solidarity-tax-credit/) of your Quebec tax return. You have up to 4 years to claim it. [51]

Also known as: Prime au travail, with the adapted work premium and the supplement
Who runs it: Revenu Québec – Revenu Québec (Government of Quebec). [52]
What it is: Refundable tax credits for workers with low income in Quebec, similar to the federal Canada workers benefit. [52]
Who it's for: You lived in Quebec on December 31. [53]; Full-time students cannot get it, unless they are a parent living with their child. [54]; The adapted premium is for people with a severely limited capacity for employment. [53]
Approximate amounts: 2026 maximum: $1,207.33 for a person living alone, $1,882.45 for a couple without children, $3,122.40 for a single parent, $4,057 for a couple with a child. [52]; Adapted premium: up to $5,234 (2026). [52]; Supplement: $200 a month for up to 12 months. [52]
Payment details: Once a year, when you file. You can ask for part of it in advance (50% if you have a dependent child, 75% if not). [52]

Who runs it: Revenu Québec – Revenu Québec (Government of Quebec). [55]
What it is: A refundable credit for seniors 70 and older with low income. [55]
Who it's for: You (or your eligible spouse) were 70 or older on December 31, 2025, and you lived in Quebec. [56]; You or your spouse is a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, protected person, or temporary resident who has lived in Canada for the last 18 months. [56]; The amount goes down by 5.40% of family income above $27,835 (single) or $45,270 (couple). [55]
Approximate amounts: Up to $2,000 for one person, or $4,000 for a couple if both are 70 or older and eligible. [55]
Payment details: Once a year, after you file. [55]
Application details: File your Quebec tax return. The credit is calculated from it. [55]

Who runs it: Revenu Québec – Revenu Québec (Government of Quebec). [57]
What it is: A credit that encourages workers 65 and older to keep working. [57]
Who it's for: You were 65 or older and lived in Quebec on December 31, 2025. [57]; Your eligible work income was more than $7,500. [57]; The credit goes down by 7% of net income above $56,500, and you get nothing at $81,500 or more. [57]
Taxable details: Not income. It lowers the tax you owe. [57]
Payment details: Once a year, on your tax return. [57]
Application details: Fill out form TP-752.PC-V and enter the result on line 391 of your Quebec return. See Revenu Québec's page (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/citizens/tax-credits/tax-credit-for-career-extension/). [57]
